title: [Chapitre] V. Algèbre des figures : notes manuscrites (14/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 22-25): in a fixed set L, a 'figure' F is a set of pairwise disjoint nonempty subsets of L (its cells). Its support is |F|, the union of the cells. F carries an order on its cells (incidence/closure), and hence an Alexandrov-type topology. Page 23 shows that a refinement F of G with |F| = |G| is exactly a refinement that is maximal among refinements of G. Such an F is a subdivision of G.

This page:
(1) Notation F ≼ G for 'F is a subdivision of G'. Grothendieck notes that ≼ is again an order relation on the set 𝔍 of figures.
(2) NB: a pair F, G with F refining G amounts to a commutative square of sets
- S = |F| ⊂ T = |G| ⊂ L, with inclusion i: S → T;
- surjections p: S → I (I = F as a set of cells, p sending a point to its cell) and q: T → J (J = G);
- an increasing map of ordered sets φ: I → J, sending a cell of F to the cell of G containing it. φ is not necessarily surjective; the marginal parenthesis likely says so.
- p and q are 'semi-continuous', i.e. continuous for the Alexandrov topologies on the posets I and J.
Give S and T the topologies pulled back from I and J along p and q. Then i is continuous.
(3) Saturated subsets: the inverse image under i of a G-saturated subset of T is an F-saturated subset of S. This reduces to the map J' ↦ φ^{-1}(J') on subsets of J and I.
(4) The page breaks off at 'L'image directe d'une partie fermée…', presumably heading to: the direct image of a closed set is closed under local finiteness or surjectivity hypotheses. The next page begins '(surj., surj. loc. fin.) ⇒ …'. Page 25 specialises to S = T, where a subdivision is a factorisation S → I → J of the stratification map through a surjective monotone φ. It then proves that F raffine G iff F ≤ G' ≼ G for some subdivision G' of G.

In modern terms: a figure is a poset-stratified subset of L, i.e. a surjection onto a poset that is continuous for the Alexandrov topology. A refinement is a morphism of stratified spaces over a monotone map of posets, with the source a subspace of the target. A subdivision is a refinement of the stratification of the same underlying space. Purpose: building a combinatorial 'algebra of figures', a tame-topology/stratification calculus, presumably for the polyhedral and 'dessin' programme announced in the Esquisse.
errors: Continuity of i for the pulled-back topologies needs commutativity q∘i = φ∘p and monotonicity of φ; both are implicit and fine.
The saturation statement is immediate from commutativity: i^{-1}(q^{-1}(J')) = p^{-1}(φ^{-1}(J')).
The direct-image claim is left unfinished. It needs extra hypotheses (surjectivity, local finiteness), as the next page indicates.

ideas.what: Subdivision order F ≼ G on figures (refinement with equal support), shown to be a partial order
ideas.where_published: Tame topology programme only sketched in Esquisse d'un programme (1984), without this formalism

ideas.what: Encoding a figure as a surjection from its support to a poset of cells, continuous for the Alexandrov topology; a refinement as a commutative square over a monotone map of posets
ideas.modern_name: poset-stratified space and morphism of stratified spaces
ideas.usually_credited_to: Alexandrov (finite topologies); modern formulation Lurie (Higher Algebra, App. A), Barwick–Glasman–Haine (Exodromy)
ideas.where_published: Ideas about stratified 'tame' structures appear in Esquisse d'un programme §5-6, not in this form

ideas.what: Saturated subsets pull back along refinements, reflected by φ^{-1} on subsets of cell posets
ideas.modern_name: pullback of constructible/saturated sets along stratified maps

deep.surprise_reason: Routine foundational bookkeeping: the order on figures and the translation of refinement into a square of Alexandrov-continuous maps to posets. This is standard poset-stratification material with nothing beyond the literature on this page.
transcription_corrections: 'avec F suffisant G' should probably read 'avec F raffinant G'.
The parenthesis after 'semi-continues' likely reads '(φ pas néc. surjective)', not '(q pr. inv. surjection)'.
'les top. compat. sur S, T définies par leurs prédécesseurs' is probably 'les top. canoniques sur S, T définies par leurs projections (images inverses des top. sur I, J)'.
'cette notion se vérifie : la relation J' ↦ φ^{-1}(J')' is roughly 'cette notion se traduit par l'application J' ↦ φ^{-1}(J') au niveau des parties de J, I'.
'sur 𝒥' is the set of figures (script J).
